Collins, Ph.D. | author-link = California Lutheran University | date = 2007-08-09 | work = Photographs of succulents | publisher = California Lutheran University }} or in [[Spanish (language)|Spanish]] '''{{Lang|es|cardón}}''',{{Cite book |last1=Bramwell |first1=David |last2=Bramwell |first2=Zoë |year=2001 |title=Wild Flowers of the Canary Islands |edition=2nd |location=Madrid |publisher=Rueda |isbn=978-84-7207-129-2 |name-list-style=amp |page=206}}{{rp|206}} is a [[succulent]] member of the genus ''[[Euphorbia]]'' and family [[Euphorbiaceae]] [[endemic]] to the [[Canary Islands]].{{cite web |url = http://www.canaryislandflora.com/arid.htm |title = Canary Islands Flora - Arid Habitat |access-date = 2008-03-02 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080306042504/http://www.canaryislandflora.com/arid.htm |archive-date = 2008-03-06 }} It is the plant symbol of the island of [[Gran Canaria]].{{cite act |type=Ley |index=7/1991 |date=30 April 1991 |title=Símbolos de la naturaleza para las Islas Canarias |trans-title=Natural Symbols for the Canary Islands |url=https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1991-16276 |language=es |via=[[Boletín Oficial del Estado|BOE]] |volume=151 |pages=20946–20497}} ==Description== The Canary Island spurge is a succulent shrub, growing to between {{convert|3|and|4|m|ft|0}} high. It is made up of fleshy quadrangular or pentagonal trunks that look like cacti. It has no leaves, instead bearing spines {{convert|5|to|14|mm|in}} long. It produces reddish-green flowers. It is [[Hardiness (plants)|hardy]] to {{convert|-2|°C|°F|sigfig=2|lk=on}}.{{cite web | url = http://www.tuin-thijs.com/euphorbia-engels.htm | title = Euphorbia | access-date = 2008-03-23 | author = Thijs de Graaf | work = euphorbia engels }} The [[latex]], which contains [[diterpenes]]{{cite journal | author =Marco, J.A. | author2 =Sanz Cervera, J.F. | author3 =Yuste, A. | title =Ingenane and lathyrane diterpenes from the latex of Euphorbia canariensis. | journal =Phytochemistry-Oxford | volume =45 | issue =3 | pages =563–570 | url =https://ods.od.nih.gov/Research/PubMed_Dietary_Supplement_Subset.aspx?mode2=detail&origin=ibids_references&therow=428571 | access-date =2008-03-23 | date =June 1997 | doi =10.1016/S0031-9422(97)00018-6 | first1 =J | bibcode =1997PChem..45..563M | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20080807031224/http://grande.nal.usda.gov/ibids/index.php?mode2=detail | archive-date =2008-08-07 | url-status =live | url-access =subscription }} is poisonous.{{cite web | url = http://florawww.eeb.uconn.edu/199200318.html | title = ''Euphorbia canariensis'' L. | access-date = 2008-03-23 | author = University of Connecticut | date = 18 March 2008 | work = EEB Greenhouse Accession Data | publisher = Ecology & Evolutionary Biology Greenhouses }} Euphorbia canariensis5 ies.jpg|Spines on a young shoot Euphorbia canariensis (Puntagorda) 01.jpg|Flowers Xrcx.jpg|Fruit [[File:Euphorbia Canariensis.jpg|thumb]] ==Distribution== The species is found on the narrow coastal belt, from sea level to {{convert|1100|m|ft}} in the Canary Islands. ==See also== * [[List of animal and plant symbols of the Canary Islands]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{Commons category-inline|Euphorbia canariensis}} *{{cite book | last = Decandolle | first = A.P. | author-link = A.
